title.zh: 卷二百 列傳第八十七: 列女一
title.raw: 卷二百 列傳第八十七: 列女一 Volume 200 Biographies 87: Exemplary Women 1

sentences.zh: 古者女子之居室也，必有傅姆師保為陳詩書圖史以訓之。

translations.literal: In antiquity, in a woman's dwelling there would always be nurse-governesses and tutors who would present poetry, books, charts, and histories to instruct her.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, a girl's household quarters would always include nurse-governesses and tutors who laid out poetry, books, maps, and histories for her instruction.

sentences.zh: 凡左右佩服之儀，內外授受之別，與所以事父母舅姑之道，蓋無所不備也。

translations.literal: As for the rituals of adornments worn left and right, the distinctions of giving and receiving between inner and outer quarters, and the ways of serving parents and parents-in-law, there was nothing left unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: The rites governing jewelry and dress, the rules separating inner from outer quarters in exchanges between men and women, and the conduct owed to parents and parents-in-law—all of this was taught in full.

sentences.zh: 而又有天子之后妃，諸侯之夫人，躬行於上，以率化之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the empresses and consorts of the Son of Heaven and the wives of feudal lords personally practiced these norms at the top to lead and transform others.
translations.idiomatic: Above them, empresses and consorts of the Son of Heaven and the wives of feudal lords embodied these standards themselves, setting an example from which others took their cue.

sentences.zh: 則其居安而有淑順之稱，臨變而有貞特之操者，夫豈偶然哉。

translations.literal: Thus those who in peace were called virtuous and compliant and who in crisis showed steadfast integrity—how could this have been mere chance?
translations.idiomatic: That women earned reputations for grace and obedience in ordinary times and showed unwavering resolve in crisis was surely no accident.

sentences.zh: 後世此道既廢，女生而處閨闥之中，溺情愛之私，耳不聆箴史之言，目不睹防範之具，由是動逾禮則，而往往自放於邪僻矣。

translations.literal: Later ages, once this practice was abandoned, girls were born and lived within inner chambers, drowning in private passions of affection, their ears not hearing words of admonition from histories, their eyes not seeing instruments of restraint; thus when they moved they transgressed ritual norms and often let themselves loose into depravity.
translations.idiomatic: After later ages abandoned this discipline, girls grew up shut in inner quarters, absorbed in private attachments, never hearing the admonitions of the classics, never seeing the safeguards of proper training—and so they routinely overstepped ritual propriety and often drifted into wayward conduct.

sentences.zh: 苟於是時而有能以懿節自著者焉，非其生質之美，則亦豈易致哉。

translations.literal: If at such a time someone could distinguish herself by admirable integrity, unless her innate character was excellent, how could it have been easily achieved?
translations.idiomatic: When a woman in such an age nonetheless distinguished herself by exemplary constancy, it was either because her nature was exceptional or because such virtue was anything but easy to attain.

sentences.zh: 史氏之書，所以必錄而弗敢略也。

translations.literal: This is why the books of the historians must record them and dare not omit them.
translations.idiomatic: That is why historical chronicles insist on recording such women and dare not pass them over.

sentences.zh: 元受命百餘年，女婦之能以行聞於朝者多矣，不能盡書，採其尤卓異者，具載於篇。

translations.literal: The Yuan received the Mandate for more than a hundred years; many women whose conduct was known at court cannot all be written; selecting those most exceptionally outstanding, they are fully recorded in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: In the more than a century since the Yuan received the Mandate, many women whose conduct won notice at court cannot all be recorded; those selected here are the most remarkable cases, set down in full in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 其間有不忍夫死，感慨自殺以從之者，雖或失於過中，然較於苟生受辱與更適而不知愧者，有間矣。

translations.literal: Among them were those who could not bear their husbands' death and, stirred by feeling, killed themselves to follow them; although this sometimes missed the mean, yet compared with those who clung to life in disgrace or remarried without shame, there is a distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Some among them, unable to bear their husbands' deaths, took their own lives in grief to join them in death; though this may sometimes overshoot the mean, it is still not the same as clinging to life in dishonor or remarrying without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 故特著之，以示勸勵之義云。

translations.literal: Therefore they are specially set forth to display the meaning of exhortation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: They are singled out here to illustrate the principle of moral encouragement.

sentences.zh: 崔氏，周術忽妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Cui was the wife of Zhou Shuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui was the wife of Zhou Shuhu.

sentences.zh: 丁亥歲，從術忽官平陽。

translations.literal: In the dinghai year she followed Shuhu to his post at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the dinghai year she accompanied Shuhu to his post at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 金將來攻城，克之，下令官屬妻子敢匿者死。

translations.literal: A Jin general came to besiege the city, captured it, and ordered that any official who dared conceal his wife would be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: A Jin general besieged and captured the city, then decreed death for any official who dared hide his wife.

sentences.zh: 時術忽以使事在上黨，崔氏急即抱幼子禎以詭計自言於將，將信之，使軍吏書其臂出之。

translations.literal: At that time Shuhu was away on a mission in Shangdang; Lady Cui hurriedly took her young son Zhen and, by a stratagem, presented herself to the general; the general believed her and had a military officer mark her arm and let her out.
translations.idiomatic: Shuhu was away on mission in Shangdang at the time. Lady Cui quickly took her young son Zhen, used a ruse to present herself to the general, won his trust, and had a clerk mark her arm so she could leave the city.

sentences.zh: 崔氏曰：「婦人臂使人執而書，非禮也。」

translations.literal: Lady Cui said: "For a woman's arm to be seized and written upon by another is not according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui said, "It is contrary to ritual for another man to seize a woman's arm and write on it."

sentences.zh: 以金賂吏，使書之紙。

translations.literal: She bribed the officer with gold to have it written on paper.
translations.idiomatic: She bribed the clerk with gold to have the mark made on paper instead.

sentences.zh: 吏曰：「吾知汝誠賢婦，然令不敢違。」

translations.literal: The officer said: "I know you are truly a virtuous wife, yet I dare not disobey the order."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk said, "I know you are a truly virtuous wife, but I dare not disobey the order."

sentences.zh: 命崔自揎袖，吏懸筆而書焉。

translations.literal: He ordered Lady Cui to roll up her own sleeve; the officer suspended the brush and wrote thus.
translations.idiomatic: He had Lady Cui roll up her own sleeve while he held the brush suspended and wrote the mark.

sentences.zh: 既出，有言其詐者，將怒，命追之。

translations.literal: After she had left, someone said she had used deception; the general was angry and ordered her pursued.
translations.idiomatic: After she escaped, someone accused her of fraud; the general grew angry and ordered her pursued.

sentences.zh: 崔與禎伏土窖三日，得免，既與術忽會。

translations.literal: Lady Cui and Zhen hid in an earthen cellar for three days and escaped; afterward they reunited with Shuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui and Zhen hid in an underground cellar for three days and escaped capture, then rejoined Shuhu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，術忽以病亡，崔年二十九，即大慟柩前，誓不更嫁，斥去麗飾，服皁布弊衣，放散婢僕，躬自紡績，悉以資產遺親舊。

translations.literal: Before long Shuhu died of illness; Cui was twenty-nine and immediately wailed greatly before the coffin, vowed never to remarry, cast off beautiful adornments, wore coarse black cloth and worn garments, released servants, personally spun and wove, and gave all her property to relatives and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shuhu died of illness. Cui was twenty-nine. She wailed bitterly before his coffin, swore never to remarry, cast off fine adornments, wore plain black cloth in shabby dress, dismissed her servants, spun and wove with her own hands, and gave away all her property to relatives and friends.

sentences.zh: 有權貴使人諷求娶，輒自爬毀其面不欲生。

translations.literal: Powerful nobles sent agents to suggest marriage proposals; she would scratch and disfigure her face, not wishing to live.
translations.idiomatic: When powerful men sent intermediaries to propose marriage, she would scratch and disfigure her face, preferring death to compliance.

sentences.zh: 四十年未嘗妄言笑，預吉會。

translations.literal: For forty years she never spoke or laughed lightly, and never participated in auspicious gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: For forty years she never spoke or laughed without cause, and never took part in auspicious gatherings.

sentences.zh: 治家教子有法，人比古烈婦云。

translations.literal: She governed the household and taught her son with method; people compared her to exemplary women of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: She ran her household and raised her son with disciplined method; people compared her to the exemplary widows of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 周氏，平灤石城人。

translations.literal: Lady Zhou was a native of Shicheng in Pingluan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou was from Shicheng in Pingluan.

sentences.zh: 年十六，適李伯通，生一子，名易。

translations.literal: At sixteen she married Li Botong and bore one son named Yi.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen she married Li Botong and bore a son named Yi.

sentences.zh: 金末，伯通監豐潤縣，國兵攻之，城破，不知所終。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin, Botong supervised Fengrun County; the national army attacked it, the city fell, and his end was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jin dynasty Botong served as overseer of Fengrun County. When the Mongol army attacked, the city fell and he was never heard from again.

sentences.zh: 周氏與易被虜，謂偕行者曰：「人苟愛其生，萬一受辱，不如死也。」

translations.literal: Lady Zhou and Yi were captured; she said to those traveling with her: "If one cherishes one's life, should one by chance suffer disgrace, better to die."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou and Yi were taken captive. She told those traveling with her, "If you value your life, consider that the slightest dishonor is worse than death."

sentences.zh: 即自投於塹。

translations.literal: She immediately threw herself into a trench.
translations.idiomatic: She immediately threw herself into a ditch.

sentences.zh: 主者怒，拔佩刀三刃其體而去，得不死。

translations.literal: Her captor was angry, drew his belt knife and slashed her body three times, then left; she did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Her captor drew his belt knife in anger, slashed her body three times, and left her for dead—but she survived.

sentences.zh: 遂攜易而逃，間關至汴，績紝以自給，教易讀書有成。

translations.literal: She then fled with Yi, traveled hard roads to Bian, supported herself by spinning hemp, and taught Yi to read until he achieved success.
translations.idiomatic: She fled with Yi, made the arduous journey to Bian, supported herself by spinning, and taught Yi to read until he succeeded in his studies.

sentences.zh: 楊氏，東平須城人。

translations.literal: Lady Yang was a native of Xucheng in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang was from Xucheng in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 夫郭三，從軍襄陽，楊氏留事舅姑，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Her husband Guo San followed the army to Xiangyang; Lady Yang remained to serve her parents-in-law and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband Guo San followed the army to Xiangyang; Lady Yang remained to serve her parents-in-law and was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，夫死戍所，母欲奪嫁之，楊氏號痛自誓，乃已。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan her husband died at the garrison; his mother wished to force her to remarry; Lady Yang wailed and pledged herself, and the plan ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan her husband died at the garrison. His mother wished to force her to remarry, but Lady Yang wailed and swore an oath, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 久之，夫骨還，舅曰：「新婦年少，終必他適，可令吾子鰥處地下耶！」

translations.literal: After a long time her husband's bones returned; her father-in-law said: "The new bride is young and will eventually marry another—shall we let my son lie widowed underground?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long time her husband's bones were brought home. Her father-in-law said, "The young bride will surely marry again one day—shall we leave my son a widower in the grave?"

sentences.zh: 將求里人亡女骨合瘞之。

translations.literal: He was about to seek the bones of a deceased girl from the village to bury them together with his son.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to seek the bones of a deceased girl from the village to bury together with his son.

sentences.zh: 楊氏聞，益悲，不食五日，自經死，遂與夫共葬焉。

translations.literal: Lady Yang heard this, grew still more grief-stricken, ate nothing for five days, hanged herself, and was buried together with her husband.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Yang heard this, her grief deepened. She ate nothing for five days, hanged herself, and was buried together with her husband.

sentences.zh: 胡烈婦，渤海劉平妻也。

translations.literal: The fierce widow Hu was the wife of Liu Ping of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: The fierce widow Hu was the wife of Liu Ping of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，平當戍棗陽，車載其家以行。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan Ping was to garrison Zaoyang and took his family by cart.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan Ping was posted to garrison Zaoyang and took his family along by cart.

sentences.zh: 夜宿沙河傍，有虎至，銜平去。

translations.literal: They lodged at night beside the Sha River; a tiger came and seized Ping away in its mouth.
translations.idiomatic: One night they camped beside the Sha River. A tiger came and carried Ping off in its jaws.

sentences.zh: 胡覺起追及之，持虎足，顧呼車中兒，取刀殺虎，虎死，扶平還至季陽城求醫，以傷卒。

translations.literal: Hu awoke, pursued and caught up, seized the tiger's foot, turned and called to the child in the cart to take a knife and kill the tiger; when the tiger died she helped Ping back to Jiyang city for medical treatment, but he died of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Hu woke, pursued the tiger, seized its foot, and called to the child in the cart to take a knife and kill it. When the tiger was dead she helped Ping back to Jiyang for treatment, but he died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 縣官言狀，命卹其母子，仍旌異之。

translations.literal: The county officials reported the circumstances; they were ordered condolence payments for mother and child, and she was further honored with special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: County officials reported what had happened. The court ordered relief for mother and child and granted her special commendation.

sentences.zh: 至大間，建德王氏女，父出耘舍傍，遇豹，為所噬，曳之升山。

translations.literal: During the Zhida period, the Wang family's daughter of Jiande—her father went out to hoe beside his hut, met a leopard, was seized and bitten by it, and it dragged him up the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhida period, a Wang family daughter of Jiande—her father went out to hoe beside his hut, met a leopard, was seized and bitten, and dragged up the mountain.

sentences.zh: 父大呼，女識父聲，驚趨救，以父所棄鋤擊豹腦，殺之，父乃得生。

translations.literal: The father shouted loudly; the daughter recognized her father's voice, ran in alarm to rescue him, took the hoe her father had dropped and struck the leopard's head, killed it, and her father was saved.
translations.idiomatic: The father shouted. The daughter recognized his voice, ran to rescue him, took up the hoe he had dropped, struck the leopard's head, and killed it—and her father lived.

sentences.zh: 闞文興妻王氏，名醜醜，建康人也。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Kan Wenxing, named Chouchou, was a native of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, wife of Kan Wenxing, called Chouchou, was from Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 文興從軍漳州，為其萬戶府知事，王氏與俱行。

translations.literal: Wenxing followed the army to Zhangzhou as clerk of its wanhu office; Wang accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxing went to Zhangzhou with the army as clerk of the wanhu office, and Wang went with him.

sentences.zh: 至元十七年，陳吊眼作亂，攻漳州，文興率兵與戰，死之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhiyuan Chen Diaoyan rebelled and attacked Zhangzhou; Wenxing led troops to fight and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Zhiyuan Chen Diaoyan rebelled and attacked Zhangzhou. Wenxing led troops against him and was killed.

sentences.zh: 王氏被掠，義不受辱，乃紿賊曰：「俟吾葬夫，即汝從也。」

translations.literal: Wang was seized but, on principle, would not accept dishonor; she deceived the bandits saying: "Wait until I bury my husband, then I will follow you."
translations.idiomatic: Wang was captured but refused on principle to suffer dishonor. She deceived the rebels, saying, "Wait until I bury my husband, and then I will follow you."

sentences.zh: 賊許之，遂脫，得負屍還，積薪焚之。

translations.literal: The bandits agreed; she escaped, was able to carry the corpse back, heaped fuel and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels agreed. She got free, carried her husband's body back, heaped fuel, and burned it.

sentences.zh: 火既熾，即自投火中死。

translations.literal: When the fire was blazing she threw herself into it and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the flames were high she threw herself into the fire and died.

sentences.zh: 至順三年，事聞，贈文興侯爵，諡曰英烈；

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhishun the matter was reported; Wenxing was posthumously granted marquis rank with the posthumous title Fierce and Loyal;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhishun the matter reached the court. Wenxing was posthumously enfeoffed as marquis with the posthumous title Fierce and Loyal;

sentences.zh: 王氏曰貞烈夫人。

translations.literal: Wang was styled the Lady of Chaste Fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was given the title Lady of Chaste Fierceness.

sentences.zh: 有司為立廟祀之，號「雙節」云。

translations.literal: The authorities built a temple to worship them, called "Double Integrity."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities built a temple to honor them, called "Double Integrity."

sentences.zh: 郎氏，湖州安吉人，宋進士朱甲妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Lang of Anji in Huzhou was the wife of Zhu Jia, a Song jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lang of Anji in Huzhou was the wife of Zhu Jia, a Song jinshi.

sentences.zh: 朱嘗仕浙東，以郎氏從。

translations.literal: Zhu once served in eastern Zhejiang, with Lady Lang accompanying him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu once served in eastern Zhejiang, and Lady Lang accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 至元間，朱歿，郎氏護喪還至玉山里，留居避盜。

translations.literal: During the Zhiyuan era Zhu died; Lady Lang escorted the coffin back to Yushan village and stayed there to avoid bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan era Zhu died. Lady Lang escorted his coffin back to Yushan village and stayed there to avoid bandits.

sentences.zh: 勢家柳氏欲強聘之，郎誓不從，夜棄裝奉柩遁。

translations.literal: The powerful Liu clan wished to force a marriage; Lang swore she would not comply, abandoned her baggage at night and fled escorting the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful Liu family wished to force her into marriage. Lang swore she would not comply, abandoned her baggage by night, and fled escorting the coffin.

sentences.zh: 柳邀之中道，复死拒，得免。

translations.literal: Liu intercepted her on the road; she again resisted to the death and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Liu intercepted her on the road; she again resisted to the death and escaped.

sentences.zh: 家居，養姑甚謹。

translations.literal: At home she nourished her mother-in-law with great care.
translations.idiomatic: At home she cared for her mother-in-law with great devotion.

sentences.zh: 姑嘗病，郎禱天，刲股肉進啖而愈。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law was ill, Lang prayed to Heaven, cut flesh from her thigh and offered it for her to eat, and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell ill, Lang prayed to Heaven, cut flesh from her thigh for her to eat, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 後姑喪，以哀聞。

translations.literal: Later when her mother-in-law died, her grief was noted.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law later died, her grief was widely noted.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，旌美之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade she was commended for her virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Dade she was commended for her virtue.

sentences.zh: 又有東平鄭氏、大寧杜氏、安西楊氏，並少寡守志，割體肉療姑病。

translations.literal: There were also the Zheng clan of Dongping, the Du clan of Daning, and the Yang clan of Anxi—all young widows who kept their resolve and cut flesh from their bodies to treat their mothers-in-law's illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Zheng family of Dongping, the Du family of Daning, and the Yang family of Anxi—all young widows who kept their resolve and cut flesh from their bodies to treat their mothers-in-law's illnesses.

sentences.zh: 秦氏二女，河南宜陽人，逸其名。

translations.literal: The two daughters of the Qin clan, natives of Yiyang in Henan—their names are lost.
translations.idiomatic: The two daughters of the Qin family, from Yiyang in Henan—their names are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 父嘗有危疾，醫云不可攻。

translations.literal: Their father once had a critical illness; physicians said it could not be treated.
translations.idiomatic: Their father once fell critically ill; physicians said it could not be treated.

sentences.zh: 姊閉戶默禱，鑿己腦和藥進飲，遂愈。

translations.literal: The elder sister closed the door and prayed silently, scooped from her own brain and mixed it with medicine for him to drink, and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The elder sister shut herself in, prayed in silence, scooped matter from her own skull, mixed it with medicine, and gave it to him to drink—and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 父後復病欲絕，妹刲股肉置粥中，父小啜即蘇。

translations.literal: Later their father fell ill again near death; the younger sister cut flesh from her thigh and placed it in porridge; the father took a small sip and revived.
translations.idiomatic: Later their father fell ill again near death. The younger sister cut flesh from her thigh and put it in porridge; he took a small sip and revived.

sentences.zh: 孫氏女，河間人。

translations.literal: The daughter of the Sun clan was from Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun family daughter was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 父病癩十年，女禱於天，求以身代，且吮其膿血，旬月而愈。

translations.literal: Her father had leprosy for ten years; the daughter prayed to Heaven to substitute her own body, also sucked his pus and blood, and in a month and more he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Her father had leprosy for ten years. The daughter prayed to Heaven to take his place, sucked his pus and blood, and within a month he recovered.

sentences.zh: 許氏女，安豐人。

translations.literal: The daughter of the Xu clan was from Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu family daughter was from Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 父疾，割股啖之乃痊。

translations.literal: When her father was ill she cut flesh from her thigh for him to eat and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When her father fell ill she cut flesh from her thigh for him to eat, and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 張氏女，廬州人，嫁為高垕妻。

translations.literal: The daughter of the Zhang clan of Luzhou married Gao Hou as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang family daughter of Luzhou married Gao Hou.

sentences.zh: 母病目喪明，張氏歸省，抱母泣，以舌舐之，目忽能視。

translations.literal: Her mother fell ill and lost her sight; Zhang returned on a visit, embraced her mother and wept, licked her eyes with her tongue, and the eyes suddenly could see.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother fell ill and lost her sight. Zhang returned on a visit, embraced her mother and wept, licked her eyes with her tongue, and her sight was suddenly restored.

sentences.zh: 州縣各以狀聞，褒表之。

translations.literal: Each prefecture and county reported the circumstances and commended them.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture and county reported these cases and commended them.

sentences.zh: 焦氏，涇陽袁天祐妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Jiao was the wife of Yuan Tianyou of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiao was the wife of Yuan Tianyou of Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 天祐祖、父始皆從軍役，祖母楊氏、母焦氏並家居守志。

translations.literal: Tianyou's grandfather and father from the start all followed military service; grandmother Lady Yang and mother Lady Jiao both kept to their homes and upheld their resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou's grandfather and father had both served in the army from the start; his grandmother Lady Yang and his mother Lady Jiao both remained at home and kept their chastity.

sentences.zh: 至元二十三年，天祐復從徵死甘州，妻焦氏年少，宗族欲改嫁之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan Tianyou again followed a campaign and died at Ganzhou; his wife Lady Jiao was young and the clan wished to have her remarry.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan Tianyou again joined a campaign and died at Ganzhou. His wife Lady Jiao was young, and the clan wished to have her remarry.

sentences.zh: 焦氏哭且言曰：「袁氏不幸三世早寡，自祖姑以來，皆守節義，豈可至吾而遂廢乎！

translations.literal: Lady Jiao wept and said: "The Yuan clan has been unfortunate—three generations of early widowhood; from the great-grandmother-in-law onward all upheld chastity and righteousness—how can this end with me!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiao wept and said, "The Yuan family has been unfortunate—three generations of early widowhood. From my husband's grandmother onward all have kept their chastity. How can I be the one to break it!

sentences.zh: 吾生為袁氏婦，死則葬袁氏土爾，終不能改容事他人也。」

translations.literal: I was born a wife of the Yuan clan; when I die I shall be buried in Yuan clan earth— I can never change my face to serve another."
translations.idiomatic: I was born a wife of the Yuan clan; when I die I shall be buried in Yuan soil. I can never change my face to serve another."

sentences.zh: 眾不敢復言。

translations.literal: The crowd dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak of it again.

sentences.zh: 周氏，澤州人，嫁為安西張興祖妻。

translations.literal: Lady Zhou was from Zezhou and married Zhang Xingzu of Anxi as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou was from Zezhou and married Zhang Xingzu of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 年二十四，興祖歿，舅姑欲使再適，周氏弗從，曰：「妾家祖、父皆早世，妾祖母、妾母並以貞操聞，妾或中道易節，是忘故夫而辱先人也。

translations.literal: At twenty-four Xingzu died; her parents-in-law wished her to remarry; Lady Zhou would not comply, saying: "In my family grandfather and father both died young; my grandmother and my mother were both known for chaste conduct—if I changed my resolve mid-course I would forget my former husband and disgrace my ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four Xingzu died. Her parents-in-law wished her to remarry, but Lady Zhou refused, saying, "In my family grandfather and father both died young. My grandmother and my mother were both known for chastity. If I changed my resolve mid-course I would forget my husband and disgrace my ancestors.

sentences.zh: 夫忘故夫不義，辱先人不孝，不孝不義，妾不為也。」

translations.literal: To forget one's former husband is unrighteous; to disgrace one's ancestors is unfilial—unfilial and unrighteous—I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: To forget one's husband is unrighteous; to disgrace one's ancestors is unfilial. I will not be unfilial and unrighteous."

sentences.zh: 遂居嫠三十年，奉舅姑，生事死葬無違禮。

translations.literal: She then lived as widow thirty years, served her parents-in-law, and in life and death observed ritual without violation.
translations.idiomatic: She lived as a widow for thirty years, served her parents-in-law, and in life and death observed ritual without fail.

sentences.zh: 其父與外祖皆無後，葬祭之禮亦周氏主之。

translations.literal: Her father and maternal grandfather both had no heirs; burial and sacrifice rites were also directed by Lady Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her father and maternal grandfather both had no male heirs; burial and sacrifice were also directed by Lady Zhou.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，並賜旌異。

translations.literal: The authorities reported these and all were granted special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported these cases and all were granted special commendation.

sentences.zh: 趙孝婦，德安應城人。

translations.literal: The filial widow Zhao was from Yingcheng in De'an.
translations.idiomatic: The filial widow Zhao was from Yingcheng in De'an.

sentences.zh: 早寡，事姑孝。

translations.literal: She was widowed early and served her mother-in-law filially.
translations.idiomatic: She was widowed young and served her mother-in-law with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 家貧，傭織於人，得美食必持歸奉姑，自啖粗糲不厭。

translations.literal: The family was poor; she hired out her weaving; whenever she obtained fine food she always brought it back for her mother-in-law while she herself ate coarse grain without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor. She hired out her weaving; whenever she obtained fine food she brought it home for her mother-in-law while she herself ate coarse fare without complaint.

sentences.zh: 嘗念姑老，一旦有不諱，無由得棺，乃以次子鬻富家，得錢百緡，買杉木治之。

translations.literal: She once reflected that her mother-in-law was old and if something happened unexpectedly there would be no way to obtain a coffin; she therefore sold her second son to a wealthy family, obtained a hundred strings of cash, and bought cedar to prepare one.
translations.idiomatic: She once thought that her mother-in-law was old and that if death came suddenly there would be no coffin. She sold her second son to a wealthy family for a hundred strings of cash and bought cedar to make one.

sentences.zh: 棺成，置於家。

translations.literal: When the coffin was finished she placed it in the home.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin was finished she kept it in the house.

sentences.zh: 南鄰失火，時南風烈甚，火勢及孝婦家，孝婦亟扶姑出避，而棺重不可移，乃撫膺大哭曰：「吾為姑賣兒得棺，無能為我救之者，苦莫大焉！」

translations.literal: The southern neighbor's house caught fire; at the time the south wind was fierce and the flames reached the filial widow's home; she hurried to support her mother-in-law out to escape, but the coffin was heavy and could not be moved; she beat her breast and wept loudly: "I sold my son for my mother-in-law to obtain this coffin—there is none who can save it for me; no suffering could be greater!"
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor to the south caught fire. The south wind was fierce and the flames reached the filial widow's home. She hurried to help her mother-in-law escape, but the coffin was too heavy to move. She beat her breast and cried, "I sold my son to buy this coffin for my mother-in-law—no one can save it now. No grief could be greater!"

sentences.zh: 言畢，風轉而北，孝婦家得不焚，人以為孝感所致。

translations.literal: When she finished speaking the wind turned northward and the filial widow's home was not burned; people attributed this to the power of filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When she had finished speaking the wind shifted northward and her home was spared. People attributed this to the power of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 霍氏二婦尹氏、楊氏，夫家鄭州人。

translations.literal: The two daughters-in-law of the Huo clan, Lady Yin and Lady Yang, were from a Zhengzhou family.
translations.idiomatic: The two daughters-in-law of the Huo family, Lady Yin and Lady Yang, were from a Zhengzhou household.

sentences.zh: 至元間，尹氏夫耀卿歿，姑命其更嫁，尹氏曰：「婦之行一節而已，再嫁而失節，妾不忍為也。」

translations.literal: During Zhiyuan Yin's husband Yaoqing died; her mother-in-law ordered her to remarry; Lady Yin said: "A wife's conduct consists in a single integrity—remarriage loses integrity; I cannot bear to do it."
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan era Yin's husband Yaoqing died. Her mother-in-law ordered her to remarry. Lady Yin said, "A wife's conduct is a single integrity. Remarriage forfeits that integrity. I cannot bear to do it."

sentences.zh: 姑曰：「世之婦皆然，人未嘗以為非，汝獨何恥之有？」

translations.literal: The mother-in-law said: "Wives of the world are all thus; people never regard it as wrong—what shame do you alone have?"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law said, "Wives everywhere do the same. No one thinks it wrong. What shame is there in it for you alone?"

sentences.zh: 尹氏曰；

translations.literal: Lady Yin said:
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin said:

sentences.zh: 「人之志不同，妾知守妾志爾。」

translations.literal: "People's resolve differs; I know only to keep my own resolve."
translations.idiomatic: "People's resolve differs. I know only to keep my own resolve."

sentences.zh: 姑不能強。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law could not compel her.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law could not force her.

sentences.zh: 楊氏夫顯卿繼歿，慮姑欲其嫁，即先白姑曰：「妾聞娣姒猶兄弟也，宜相好焉。

translations.literal: Lady Yang's husband Xianqing died in succession; fearing her mother-in-law would wish her to remarry, she first informed her mother-in-law: "I have heard that sisters-in-law are like brothers and ought to be on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang's husband Xianqing died next. Fearing her mother-in-law would wish her to remarry, she spoke to her first: "I have heard that sisters-in-law are like brothers and ought to be on good terms.

sentences.zh: 今姒既留，妾可獨去乎，願與共修婦道，以終事吾姑。」

translations.literal: Now that my elder sister-in-law is staying, how can I leave alone? I wish to cultivate wifely conduct together with her to serve my mother-in-law to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Now that my sister-in-law is staying, how can I go off alone? I wish to practice the duties of a wife together with her and serve my mother-in-law to the end."

sentences.zh: 姑曰：「汝果能若是，吾何言哉！」

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law said: "If you can truly do this, what more can I say!"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law said, "If you can truly do this, what more can I say!"

sentences.zh: 於是同處二十餘年，以節孝聞。

translations.literal: Thus they lived together for more than twenty years, renowned for integrity and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: They lived together for more than twenty years and were known for their chastity and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 又有邠州任氏、乾州田氏，皆一家一婦，俱少寡誓不他適，戮力蠶桑，以養舅姑。

translations.literal: There were also the Ren clan of Binzhou and the Tian clan of Qianzhou—each household had a single wife, all young widows who swore not to marry another, exerting themselves in sericulture to support their parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the Ren family of Binzhou and the Tian family of Qianzhou—each household had one wife, all young widows who swore never to remarry and worked together at sericulture to support their parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 事聞，並命褒表。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, all were ordered to be commended.
translations.idiomatic: When these cases were reported, all were ordered commended.

sentences.zh: 王德政妻郭氏，大名人。

translations.literal: Guo, wife of Wang Dezheng, was from Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Guo, wife of Wang Dezheng, was from Daming.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母張氏孝謹，以女儀聞於鄉。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, she served her mother Lady Zhang with filial care and was known in the village for feminine propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, she served her mother Lady Zhang with filial devotion and was known in the village for proper conduct as a woman.

sentences.zh: 及笄，富貴家慕之，爭求聘，張氏不許。

translations.literal: When she came of age, wealthy families admired her and competed to seek her hand; Zhang would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age, wealthy families admired her and competed for her hand, but Zhang would not consent.

sentences.zh: 時德政教授里中，年四十餘，貌甚古陋，張氏以貧不能教二子，欲納德政為婿，使教之。

translations.literal: At the time Dezheng taught in the village, was over forty, and his appearance was very plain and homely; Zhang, being poor and unable to educate her two sons, wished to take Dezheng as son-in-law so he could teach them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Dezheng taught in the village. He was over forty and very plain in appearance. Zhang, too poor to educate her two sons, wished to take Dezheng as a son-in-law so he could teach them.

sentences.zh: 宗族皆不然，郭氏慨然願順母志。

translations.literal: The clan all disapproved, but Guo resolutely wished to follow her mother's will.
translations.idiomatic: The clan all disapproved, but Guo resolutely agreed to follow her mother's wish.

sentences.zh: 既婚，與德政相敬如賓，囑教二弟有成。

translations.literal: After marriage she and Dezheng treated each other with the respect of guests, and charged that the two younger brothers be educated to achievement.
translations.idiomatic: After marriage she and Dezheng treated each other with the respect of guests, and urged that her two younger brothers be educated to success.

sentences.zh: 未幾德政卒，郭氏年方二十餘，勵節自守，甚有貞名。

translations.literal: Before long Dezheng died; Guo was just over twenty, encouraged her integrity and kept herself chaste, with a great reputation for fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dezheng died. Guo was just over twenty. She upheld her integrity and kept herself chaste, earning a great reputation for fidelity.

sentences.zh: 大德間表其家。

translations.literal: During the Dade era her household was commended.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era her household was commended.

sentences.zh: 只魯花真，蒙古氏。

translations.literal: Zhiluhuazhen was of the Mongol clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiluhuazhen was a Mongol woman.

sentences.zh: 年二十六，夫忽都病卒，誓不再醮，孝養舅姑。

translations.literal: At twenty-six her husband Hudu died of illness; she swore never to remarry and filially supported her parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-six her husband Hudu died of illness. She swore never to remarry and devoted herself to supporting her parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 逾二十五年，舅姑歿，塵衣垢面，廬於墓終身。

translations.literal: After more than twenty-five years her parents-in-law died; in dusty garments and a dirty face she lodged at the tomb for life.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty-five years her parents-in-law died. In dusty clothes and with a dirty face she lived at the tomb for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 至元間旌之。

translations.literal: During the Zhiyuan era she was honored with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan era she was granted official commendation.

sentences.zh: 其後，又有翼城宋仲榮妻梁氏，舅歿，負土為墳；

translations.literal: Later there was also Lady Liang, wife of Song Zhongrong of Yicheng, who when her father-in-law died carried earth to make his mound;
translations.idiomatic: Later there was also Lady Liang, wife of Song Zhongrong of Yicheng, who when her father-in-law died carried earth to build his mound;

sentences.zh: 懷孟何氏、大名趙氏，並以夫歿守志，養舅姑以壽終，親負土築其墳，高三丈餘。

translations.literal: the He clan of Huaimeng and the Zhao clan of Daming—all when their husbands died kept their resolve, nourished their parents-in-law until they died of old age, and personally carried earth to build their mounds more than three zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: the He family of Huaimeng and the Zhao family of Daming—all when their husbands died kept their resolve, supported their parents-in-law until they died of old age, and personally carried earth to build mounds more than three zhang high.

sentences.zh: 段氏，隆興霍榮妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Duan was the wife of Huo Rong of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan was the wife of Huo Rong of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 榮無子，嘗乞人為養子。

translations.literal: Rong had no son and once begged someone to be an adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had no son and once begged for someone to be adopted as his heir.

sentences.zh: 榮卒，段氏年二十六，養舅姑以孝稱。

translations.literal: When Rong died Duan was twenty-six and nourished her parents-in-law, famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died Duan was twenty-six. She supported her parents-in-law and was famed for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 舅姑歿，榮諸父仲汶貪其產，謂段曰：「汝子假子也，可令歸宗。

translations.literal: When her parents-in-law died Rong's paternal uncle Zhongwen coveted her property and said to Duan: "Your son is a borrowed son; he can be sent back to his clan.
translations.idiomatic: When her parents-in-law died Rong's paternal uncle Zhongwen coveted her property and said to Duan, "Your son is a borrowed son. He can be sent back to his clan.

sentences.zh: 汝無子，宜改適，霍氏業汝無預焉。」

translations.literal: You have no son; you should remarry; Huo family property has nothing to do with you."
translations.idiomatic: You have no son. You should remarry. The Huo family property has nothing to do with you."

sentences.zh: 段曰：「家資不可計，但再醮非義，尚容妾思之。」

translations.literal: Duan said: "Family assets cannot be counted, but remarriage is not righteous; still allow me to consider it."
translations.idiomatic: Duan said, "The family assets are beyond counting, but remarriage is not righteous. Allow me to consider it."

sentences.zh: 即退入寢室，引針刺面，墨漬之，誓死不貳。

translations.literal: She withdrew to her bedchamber, took a needle and pricked her face, stained it with ink, and swore she would die rather than take a second husband.
translations.idiomatic: She withdrew to her bedchamber, pricked her face with a needle, stained it with ink, and swore she would die rather than take a second husband.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，府上狀中書，給羊酒幣帛，仍命旌門，复役如製。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade the prefecture reported upward to the central secretariat, granting sheep, wine, silks, and cloth, and ordering an honorific gate, with corvée exemption as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dade the prefecture reported to the central secretariat. She was granted sheep, wine, silks, and cloth, an honorific gate was erected, and corvée was exempted as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 又有興和吳氏，自刺其面；

translations.literal: There was also Lady Wu of Xinghe, who pricked her own face;
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Wu of Xinghe, who pricked her own face;

sentences.zh: 成紀謝思明妻趙氏，自髡其發；

translations.literal: Zhao, wife of Xie Siming of Chenji, who shaved her own hair;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, wife of Xie Siming of Chenji, who shaved her own hair;

sentences.zh: 冀寧田濟川妻武氏、溧水曹子英妻尤氏，囓指滴血，並誓不更嫁。

translations.literal: Wu, wife of Tian Jichuan of Jining, and You, wife of Cao Ziying of Lishui, who bit their fingers and drew blood—all swore never to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, wife of Tian Jichuan of Jining, and You, wife of Cao Ziying of Lishui, who bit their fingers and drew blood—all swore never to remarry.

sentences.zh: 各以有司為請旌之。

translations.literal: Each had the authorities request commendation for them.
translations.idiomatic: In each case the authorities requested commendation on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 朱虎妻茅氏，崇明人。

translations.literal: Mao, wife of Zhu Hu, was from Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: Mao, wife of Zhu Hu, was from Chongming.

sentences.zh: 大德間，虎官都水監，坐罪籍其家，吏錄送茅氏及二子赴京師。

translations.literal: During Dade Hu served as director of the Directorate of Waterways, was convicted and his household registered for confiscation; clerks recorded and sent Lady Mao and two sons to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era Hu served as director of the Directorate of Waterways. He was convicted and his household was registered for confiscation. Clerks sent Lady Mao and her two sons to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太醫提點師甲乞歸家，欲妻之。

translations.literal: The medical superintendent of the Imperial Medical Service Shi Jia asked to take her home, wishing to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jia, medical superintendent of the Imperial Medical Service, asked to take her home, wishing to marry her.

sentences.zh: 茅氏誓死不從，母子三人以裾相結連，晝夜倚抱號哭，形貌銷毀。

translations.literal: Lady Mao swore she would rather die than comply; mother and two sons tied their skirt hems together, day and night leaned on each other and wailed, their appearance wasting away.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mao swore she would rather die than comply. Mother and sons tied their skirt hems together, leaned on each other day and night, and wailed until their bodies wasted away.

sentences.zh: 師知不可奪，釋之。

translations.literal: Shi knew he could not force her and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi knew he could not force her and released them.

sentences.zh: 茅氏托居永明尼寺，憂憤不食卒。

translations.literal: Lady Mao entrusted herself to Yongming nunnery, grieved and refused food until death.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mao took refuge at Yongming nunnery, grieved and refused food until she died.

sentences.zh: 聞氏，紹興俞新之妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Wen was the wife of Yu Xinzhi of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wen was the wife of Yu Xinzhi of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，新之歿，聞氏年尚少，父母慮其不能守，欲更嫁之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade Xinzhi died; Lady Wen was still young; her parents feared she could not keep her resolve and wished her to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dade Xinzhi died. Lady Wen was still young. Her parents feared she could not keep her resolve and wished her to remarry.

sentences.zh: 聞氏哭曰：「一身二夫，烈婦所恥。

translations.literal: Lady Wen wept: "One body, two husbands—is the shame of a fierce wife.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wen wept, "One body, two husbands—that is the shame of a fierce wife.

sentences.zh: 妾可無生，可無恥乎！

translations.literal: I can live without life, but not without shame!
translations.idiomatic: I can live without life, but not without shame!

sentences.zh: 且姑老子幼，妾去當令誰視也？」

translations.literal: Moreover my mother-in-law is old and my son is young—if I leave, who will attend them?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my mother-in-law is old and my son is young. If I leave, who will care for them?"

sentences.zh: 即斷髮自誓。

translations.literal: She cut her hair and swore an oath.
translations.idiomatic: She cut her hair and swore an oath.

sentences.zh: 父知其志篤，乃不忍強。

translations.literal: Her father knew her resolve was firm and could not bear to force her.
translations.idiomatic: Her father knew her resolve was firm and could not bear to force her.

sentences.zh: 姑久病風，且失明，聞氏手滌溷穢不怠，時漱口上堂舐其目，目為復明。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law had long been ill with wind affliction and was blind; Lady Wen by hand washed filth without slackening, at times rinsed her mouth and went to the hall to lick her eyes, and her sight was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law had long suffered from wind affliction and was blind. Lady Wen washed her filth by hand without slackening. At times she rinsed her mouth and went to the hall to lick her eyes, and her sight was restored.

sentences.zh: 及姑卒，家貧，無資傭工，與子親負土葬之，朝夕悲號，聞者慘惻。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law died the family was poor without funds to hire labor; with her son she personally carried earth to bury her; morning and evening she wailed—hearers were deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law died the family was too poor to hire labor. She and her son personally carried earth to bury her. Morning and evening she wailed, and those who heard were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 鄉里嘉其孝，為之語曰：「欲學孝婦，當問俞母。」

translations.literal: The villagers praised her filial piety and made a saying: "If you wish to learn from a filial wife, ask Lady Yu."
translations.idiomatic: The villagers praised her filial piety and said, "If you wish to learn from a filial wife, ask Lady Yu."

sentences.zh: 又有劉氏，渤海李伍妻也。

translations.literal: There was also Lady Liu, wife of Li Wu of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Liu, wife of Li Wu of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 少寡，父母使再醮，不從。

translations.literal: Widowed young, her parents urged her to remarry, but she would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, her parents urged her to remarry, but she would not comply.

sentences.zh: 舅患疽，劉禱於天，數日潰，吮其血，乃愈。

translations.literal: Her father-in-law suffered an ulcer; Liu prayed to Heaven; in several days it suppurated; she sucked the blood and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Her father-in-law suffered an ulcer. Liu prayed to Heaven. In several days it suppurated; she sucked the blood and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 既而親挽小車，載舅詣岳祠以答神貺。

translations.literal: Then she personally drew a small cart and carried her father-in-law to the Yue shrine to repay the gods' favor.
translations.idiomatic: Then she personally drew a small cart and carried her father-in-law to the Yue shrine to repay the gods' favor.

sentences.zh: 馬英，河內人，性孝友。

translations.literal: Ma Ying was from Henei, by nature filial and brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ying was from Henei and was by nature filial and brotherly.

sentences.zh: 父喪哀毀，二兄繼歿，英獨事母甚謹，又奉二寡嫂與居，使得保全嫠節。

translations.literal: At his father's death he mourned with destruction; two elder brothers died in succession; Ying alone served his mother with great care, also housed two widowed sisters-in-law together, enabling them to preserve their widowhood.
translations.idiomatic: At his father's death he mourned with utter devastation. Two elder brothers died in succession. Ying alone served his mother with great care and also housed his two widowed sisters-in-law together, enabling them to preserve their chastity.

sentences.zh: 及喪母，卜地葬諸喪，親負土為四墳，手植松柏，廬墓側終身。

translations.literal: When his mother died he divined ground to bury all the dead, personally carried earth for four mounds, planted pine and cypress by hand, and lodged beside the tombs for life.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he chose ground to bury all the dead, personally carried earth for four mounds, planted pine and cypress with his own hands, and lived beside the tombs for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 趙氏女名玉兒，冠州人。

translations.literal: The Zhao family's daughter named Yu'er was from Guanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao family daughter named Yu'er was from Guanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗許為李氏婦，未婚夫死，遂誓不嫁，以養父母。

translations.literal: Once betrothed to become the Li family's wife; before marriage her fiancé died; she swore not to marry and nourished her parents.
translations.idiomatic: She had been betrothed to the Li family, but before the marriage her fiancé died. She swore not to marry and supported her parents.

sentences.zh: 父母歿，負土為墳，鄉里稱孝焉。

translations.literal: When her parents died she carried earth for the mound; the village praised her filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When her parents died she carried earth for their mound, and the village praised her filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 馮氏，名淑安，字靜君，大名宦家女，山陰縣尹山東李如忠繼室也。

translations.literal: Feng, named Shuan, style Jingjun, was a daughter of a Daming official family and the second wife of Li Ruzhong, magistrate of Shanyin county in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shuan, styled Jingjun, was a daughter of a prominent official family and the second wife of Li Ruzhong, magistrate of Shanyin county in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 如忠初娶蒙古氏，生子任，數歲而卒。

translations.literal: Ruzhong first married a Mongol woman and they had a son named Ren; after several years she died.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhong had first married a Mongol woman and they had a son named Ren; after a few years she died.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，如忠病篤，謂馮曰：「吾已矣，其奈汝何？」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade Ruzhong was gravely ill and said to Feng: "I am finished—what will become of you?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dade Ruzhong was gravely ill and said to Feng, "I am finished. What will become of you?"

sentences.zh: 馮氏引刀斷發，自誓不他適。

translations.literal: Feng took a knife and cut her hair, swearing she would not marry another.
translations.idiomatic: Feng took a knife and cut her hair, swearing she would not marry another.

sentences.zh: 如忠歿兩月，遺腹生一子，名伏。

translations.literal: Two months after Ruzhong's death she bore a posthumous son named Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Two months after Ruzhong's death she bore a posthumous son named Fu.

sentences.zh: 李氏及蒙古氏之族在北，聞如忠歿於官，家多遺財，相率來山陰。

translations.literal: The Li clan and the Mongol clan's kin were in the north; hearing Ruzhong had died in office and the family had much remaining wealth, they came in a body to Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: The Li clan and the Mongol clan's kin were in the north. Hearing that Ruzhong had died in office and that the family had much remaining wealth, they came in a body to Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 馮氏方病，乘間盡取其貲及子任以去。

translations.literal: Feng was then ill; they seized the opportunity and took all their goods and son Ren away.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was then ill. They seized the opportunity and took all the goods and her stepson Ren away.

sentences.zh: 馮不與較，一室蕭然，唯餘如忠及蒙古氏之柩而已。

translations.literal: Feng did not contest it; one room was desolate—only Ruzhong's and the Mongol woman's coffins remained.
translations.idiomatic: Feng did not contest it. The house was left desolate—only Ruzhong's coffin and the Mongol woman's coffin remained.

sentences.zh: 朝夕哭泣，鄰里不忍聞。

translations.literal: Morning and evening she wept; neighbors could not bear to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening she wept until neighbors could not bear to hear.

sentences.zh: 久之，鬻衣權厝二柩蕺山下，攜其子廬墓側。

translations.literal: After a long time she sold clothes to provisionally bury the two coffins at Jishan, took her son, and lodged beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time she sold her clothes to provisionally bury the two coffins at Jishan, then took her son and lived beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 時年始二十二，羸形苦節，為女師以自給。

translations.literal: She was then only twenty-two, frail in form with bitter integrity, and worked as a women's teacher to support herself.
translations.idiomatic: She was then only twenty-two, frail in body but stern in integrity, and supported herself by teaching young women.

sentences.zh: 父母來視之，憐其孤苦，欲使更事人，馮爪面流血，不肯從。

translations.literal: Her parents came to see her, pitied her lonely hardship, and wished her to marry again; Feng scratched her face until it bled and would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents came to see her, pitied her lonely hardship, and wished her to marry again. Feng scratched her face until it bled and would not comply.

sentences.zh: 居二十年，始護喪歸葬汶上。

translations.literal: After dwelling twenty years she finally escorted the coffins home to bury them at Wenshang.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty years she finally escorted the coffins home for burial at Wenshang.

sentences.zh: 齊魯之人聞之，莫不嘆息。

translations.literal: People of Qi and Lu heard and none did not sigh.
translations.idiomatic: When people of Qi and Lu heard of it, none failed to sigh.

sentences.zh: 李君進妻王氏，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Li Junjin, was from Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, wife of Li Junjin, was from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 大德八年，君進病卒，卜葬，將發引，親戚鄰里咸會。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade Junjin died of illness; the burial ground was divined; when the procession was about to set out, relatives and neighbors all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dade Junjin died of illness. The burial ground was divined, and when the procession was about to set out, relatives and neighbors all gathered.

sentences.zh: 王氏謂眾曰：「夫婦死同穴，義也。

translations.literal: Wang said to the crowd: "Husband and wife die in one grave—that is righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang said to the crowd, "Husband and wife die in one grave—that is righteousness.

sentences.zh: 吾得從良人逝，不亦可乎！」

translations.literal: I can follow my good man in death—is that not acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: I can follow my husband in death—is that not acceptable!"

sentences.zh: 因撫棺大慟，嘔血升許，即僕於地死。

translations.literal: She stroked the coffin and wailed greatly, vomited more than a sheng of blood, and immediately collapsed on the ground dead.
translations.idiomatic: She stroked the coffin and wailed greatly, vomited more than a sheng of blood, and immediately collapsed dead on the ground.

sentences.zh: 眾為斂之，與夫連柩出葬，送者數百人，莫不灑泣。

translations.literal: The crowd prepared her body; she was buried in linked coffins with her husband; more than three hundred escorted them—none did not weep.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd prepared her body. She was buried in linked coffins with her husband. Several hundred people escorted them, and none failed to weep.

sentences.zh: 移剌氏，同知湖州路事耶律忽都不花妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Yila was the wife of Yelü Hudubuhua, assistant administrator of Huzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yelü was the wife of Yelü Hudubuhua, assistant administrator of Huzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 夫歿，割耳自誓。

translations.literal: When her husband died she cut her ear and swore an oath.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died she cut her ear and swore an oath.

sentences.zh: 既葬，廬墓側，悲號不食死。

translations.literal: After burial she lodged beside the tomb, wailed, and refused food until death.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial she lived beside the tomb, wailed, and refused food until she died.

sentences.zh: 趙氏名哇兒，大寧人。

translations.literal: Zhao named Wa'er was from Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, called Wa'er, was from Daning.

sentences.zh: 年二十，夫蕭氏病劇，謂哇兒曰：「我死，汝年少，若之何？」

translations.literal: At twenty her husband of the Xiao clan was gravely ill and said to Wa'er: "When I die you are young—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: At twenty her Xiao husband was gravely ill and said to Wa'er, "When I die you are young. What then?"

sentences.zh: 哇兒曰：「君幸自寬，脫有不可諱，妾不獨生，必從君地下。」

translations.literal: Wa'er said: "Husband, please ease yourself; if there is what cannot be avoided, I will not live alone—I must follow you underground."
translations.idiomatic: Wa'er said, "Husband, please ease yourself. If the worst cannot be avoided, I will not live alone. I must follow you underground."

sentences.zh: 遂命匠制巨棺。

translations.literal: She then ordered craftsmen to make a huge coffin.
translations.idiomatic: She then ordered craftsmen to make a huge coffin.

sentences.zh: 夫歿，即自經死，家人同棺斂葬焉。

translations.literal: When her husband died she immediately hanged herself; the family buried them together in the same coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died she immediately hanged herself. The family buried them together in the same coffin.

sentences.zh: 又有雷州朱克彬妻周氏，大都費岩妻王氏、買哥妻耶律氏，曹州鄭臘兒妻康氏，陝州陳某妻別娥娥，大同宋堅童妻班氏、李安童妻胡氏，晉州劉恕妻趙氏，冀寧王思忠妻張氏，饒州劉楫妻趙氏，東平徐順妻彭氏，大寧趙澐兒妻安氏、陳恭妻張氏、武壽妻劉氏、宋敬先妻謝氏、撒里妻蕭氏，古城魏貴妻周氏，任城郭灰兒妻趙氏，棗陽朱某妻丁氏，葉縣王保子妻趙氏，興州某氏妻魏氏，灤州裴某妻董貴哥，成都張保童妻郝氏，利州高塔必也妻白氏，河南楊某妻盧氏，蒙古氏太術妻阿不察、相兀孫妻脫脫真，並以早寡不忍獨生，以死從夫者。

translations.literal: There were also Lady Zhou, wife of Zhu Kebin of Leizhou; Lady Wang, wife of Fei Yan of Dadu; Lady Yelü, wife of Maige; Lady Kang, wife of Zheng La'er of Caozhou; Bie E'e, wife of a certain Chen of Shanzhou; Lady Ban, wife of Song Jiantong of Datong; Lady Hu, wife of Li Antong; Lady Zhao, wife of Liu Shu of Jinzhou; Lady Zhang, wife of Wang Sizhong of Jining; Lady Zhao, wife of Liu Ji of Raozhou; Lady Peng, wife of Xu Shun of Dongping; Lady An, wife of Zhao Yun'er of Daning; Lady Zhang, wife of Chen Gong; Lady Liu, wife of Wu Shou; Lady Xie, wife of Song Jingxian; Lady Xiao, wife of Sali; Lady Zhou, wife of Wei Gui of Gucheng; Lady Zhao, wife of Guo Hui'er of Rencheng; Lady Ding, wife of a certain Zhu of Zaoyang; Lady Zhao, wife of Wang Baozi of Yexian; Lady Wei, wife of a certain clan of Xingzhou; Dong Guige, wife of a certain Pei of Luanzhou; Lady Hao, wife of Zhang Baotong of Chengdu; Lady Bai, wife of Gao Tabiye of Lizhou; Lady Lu, wife of a certain Yang of Henan; Abucha, wife of Taishu of the Mongol clan; Tuotuozhen, wife of Xiangwusun—all widowed early, unable to bear living alone, and followed their husbands in death.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Lady Zhou, wife of Zhu Kebin of Leizhou; Lady Wang, wife of Fei Yan of Dadu; Lady Yelü, wife of Maige; Lady Kang, wife of Zheng La'er of Caozhou; Bie E'e, wife of a certain Chen of Shanzhou; Lady Ban, wife of Song Jiantong of Datong; Lady Hu, wife of Li Antong; Lady Zhao, wife of Liu Shu of Jinzhou; Lady Zhang, wife of Wang Sizhong of Jining; Lady Zhao, wife of Liu Ji of Raozhou; Lady Peng, wife of Xu Shun of Dongping; Lady An, wife of Zhao Yun'er of Daning; Lady Zhang, wife of Chen Gong; Lady Liu, wife of Wu Shou; Lady Xie, wife of Song Jingxian; Lady Xiao, wife of Sali; Lady Zhou, wife of Wei Gui of Gucheng; Lady Zhao, wife of Guo Hui'er of Rencheng; Lady Ding, wife of a certain Zhu of Zaoyang; Lady Zhao, wife of Wang Baozi of Yexian; Lady Wei, wife of a certain family of Xingzhou; Dong Guige, wife of a certain Pei of Luanzhou; Lady Hao, wife of Zhang Baotong of Chengdu; Lady Bai, wife of Gao Tabiye of Lizhou; Lady Lu, wife of a certain Yang of Henan; Abucha, wife of Taishu of the Mongol clan; and Tuotuozhen, wife of Xiangwusun—all widowed young, unable to bear living alone, and followed their husbands in death.

sentences.zh: 事聞，悉命褒表，或賜錢贈諡云。

translations.literal: When reported, all were ordered commended, and some were given cash and posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: When these cases were reported, all were ordered commended, and some were given cash and posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 朱淑信，山陰人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shuxin was from Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shuxin was from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 少寡，誓不再嫁。

translations.literal: Widowed young, she swore never to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, she swore never to remarry.

sentences.zh: 一女妙淨，幼哭父雙目並失明。

translations.literal: One daughter Miaojing, as a child wept at her father's death until both eyes went blind together.
translations.idiomatic: She had one daughter, Miaojing, who as a child wept at her father's death until both eyes went blind.

sentences.zh: 及長，擇偶者不至，家貧歲凶，母子相依，以苦節自厲。

translations.literal: When grown suitors did not come; the family was poor and years were famine-stricken; mother and daughter relied on each other, disciplining themselves with bitter integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When she grew up suitors did not come. The family was poor and famine years followed. Mother and daughter relied on each other and disciplined themselves with bitter integrity.

sentences.zh: 士人王士貴重其孝，乃求娶焉。

translations.literal: The scholar Wang Shigui prized her filial piety and then sought to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: The scholar Wang Shigui prized her filial piety and then sought to marry her.

sentences.zh: 葛妙真，宣城民家女。

translations.literal: Ge Miaozhen was a common-family daughter of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Miaozhen was a commoner's daughter of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 九歲，聞日者言，母年五十當死，妙真即悲憂祝天，誓不嫁，終身齋素，以延母年。

translations.literal: At nine years she heard a calendar-reader say her mother at fifty would die; Miaozhen immediately grieved, prayed to Heaven, swore not to marry, and kept a lifelong vegetarian fast to extend her mother's years.
translations.idiomatic: At nine she heard a calendar-reader say her mother would die at fifty. Miaozhen immediately grieved, prayed to Heaven, swore not to marry, and kept a lifelong vegetarian fast to extend her mother's life.

sentences.zh: 母後年八十一卒。

translations.literal: Her mother later died at eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother later died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 畏吾氏三女，家錢塘。

translations.literal: Three daughters of the Uighur clan; the family was in Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Three daughters of the Uighur clan lived in Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 諸兄遠仕不歸，母思之疾，三女欲慰母意，乃共斷發誓天，終身不嫁以養母，同力侍護四十餘年。

translations.literal: Elder brothers were far away in office and did not return; their mother missed them and fell ill; the three daughters wished to comfort her, together cut their hair and swore to Heaven, vowed lifelong not to marry to nourish their mother, and together served and protected her for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Their elder brothers served far away and did not return. Their mother missed them and fell ill. The three daughters wished to comfort her, cut their hair together and swore to Heaven, vowed never to marry in order to support their mother, and together cared for her for more than forty years.

sentences.zh: 母竟以壽終。

translations.literal: Their mother finally died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother finally died of old age.

sentences.zh: 事上，並賜旌異。

translations.literal: Reported upward, all were granted special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: These cases were reported upward and all were granted special commendation.

sentences.zh: 王氏，燕人張買奴妻也。

translations.literal: Wang was the wife of Zhang Maimu of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was the wife of Zhang Maimu of Yan.

sentences.zh: 年十六，買奴官錢塘病歿，葬城西十里外。

translations.literal: When she was sixteen, Maimu, serving as an official at Qiantang, died of illness; he was buried ten li west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When she was sixteen, Maimu, posted to Qiantang as an official, died of illness. He was buried ten li west of the city.

sentences.zh: 王氏每旦被髮步往奠之，伏墓大慟欲絕，久而致疾。

translations.literal: Each morning Wang let down her hair and walked to offer sacrifice, prostrated at the tomb and wailed until near death, and after long time fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning Wang went with her hair unbound to mourn at the tomb, prostrated herself and wailed until she nearly died, and after a long time fell ill.

sentences.zh: 舅姑力止其行，乃已。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law forcibly stopped her from going and she then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law forcibly stopped her from going, and she then ceased.

sentences.zh: 服闋，舅姑謂之曰：「吾子已歿，新婦年尚少，宜自圖終身計，毋徒淹吾家也。」

translations.literal: When mourning was completed her parents-in-law said to her: "Our son is already dead; the new bride is still young—you should plan for your own lifetime and not simply linger in our household."
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was completed her parents-in-law said to her, "Our son is dead and you are still young. You should plan for your own future and not simply linger in our household."

sentences.zh: 王氏泣曰：「父母命妾奉箕帚於張氏，今夫不幸早逝，天也。

translations.literal: Wang wept: "My parents commanded me to serve the Zhang clan with broom and dustpan; now my husband has unfortunately died early—that is Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: Wang wept, "My parents commanded me to serve the Zhang clan. Now my husband has died early—that is Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 此足豈可復履他人門乎！」

translations.literal: How can these feet tread another's threshold again!"
translations.idiomatic: How can these feet ever cross another man's threshold again!"

sentences.zh: 固不從。

translations.literal: She firmly would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: She firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 煢居三十年，貞白無少玷。

translations.literal: She lived alone thirty years, chaste and pure without the slightest stain.
translations.idiomatic: She lived alone for thirty years, chaste and pure without the slightest stain.

sentences.zh: 又有馮翊王義妻盧氏、睢陽劉澤妻解氏、東平楊三妻張氏，並守志有節。

translations.literal: There were also Lady Lu, wife of Wang Yi of Fengyi; Lady Xie, wife of Liu Ze of Suiyang; and Lady Zhang, wife of Yang San of Dongping—all kept their resolve with integrity.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Lady Lu, wife of Wang Yi of Fengyi; Lady Xie, wife of Liu Ze of Suiyang; and Lady Zhang, wife of Yang San of Dongping—all kept their resolve with integrity.

sentences.zh: 命旌其門。

translations.literal: They were ordered honorific gates erected.
translations.idiomatic: They were ordered honorific gates erected.

sentences.zh: 張義婦，濟南鄒平人，年十八歸里人李伍。

translations.literal: The righteous wife Zhang was from Zouping in Jinan; at eighteen she married Li Wu of her village.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous wife Zhang was from Zouping in Jinan. At eighteen she married Li Wu of her village.

sentences.zh: 伍與從子零戍福寧、未幾死戍所。

translations.literal: Wu and his nephew Ling garrisoned Funing; before long he died at the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and his nephew Ling were posted to garrison Funing. Before long he died at the garrison.

sentences.zh: 張獨家居，養舅姑甚至。

translations.literal: Zhang lived alone at home and nourished her parents-in-law with utmost devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang lived alone at home and supported her parents-in-law with utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 父母舅姑病，凡四刲股肉救不懈。

translations.literal: When parents and parents-in-law were ill she four times cut flesh from her thigh to save them without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: When her parents and parents-in-law fell ill she four times cut flesh from her thigh to save them, never slackening in her efforts.

sentences.zh: 及死，喪葬無遺禮。

translations.literal: When they died, in burial and mourning nothing of ritual was omitted.
translations.idiomatic: When they died she observed every point of burial and mourning ritual.

sentences.zh: 既而歎曰：「妾夫死數千里外，妾不能歸骨以葬者，以舅姑父母在，無所仰故也。

translations.literal: She then sighed: "My husband died several thousand li away; I could not return his bones for burial because my parents-in-law were alive and there was none on whom they could rely.
translations.idiomatic: She then sighed, "My husband died thousands of li away. I could not bring his bones home for burial because my parents-in-law were still alive and had no one else to rely on.

sentences.zh: 今不幸父母舅姑已死，而夫骨終暴棄遠土，使無妾即已，妾在，敢愛死乎！」

translations.literal: Now my parents and parents-in-law have unfortunately died, yet my husband's bones still lie exposed in distant soil. If I were not here it would be done—but while I live, how can I cherish my own life!"
translations.idiomatic: Now my parents and parents-in-law are dead, yet my husband's bones still lie exposed in distant soil. If I were not here, nothing would be done. While I live, how can I spare my own life!"

sentences.zh: 乃臥積冰上，誓曰：「天若許妾取夫骨，雖寒甚，當得不死。」

translations.literal: She lay on accumulated ice and swore: "If Heaven permits me to fetch my husband's bones, though the cold is extreme I shall not die."
translations.idiomatic: She lay on accumulated ice and swore, "If Heaven permits me to fetch my husband's bones, however bitter the cold I shall not die."

sentences.zh: 踰月，竟不死。

translations.literal: After more than a month she indeed did not die.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month she did not die.

sentences.zh: 鄉人異之，乃相率贈以錢，大書其事於衣以行。

translations.literal: The villagers marveled and together presented her money; they wrote the matter large on her garment for her journey.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers marveled and together gave her money. They wrote her story in large characters on her garment for the journey.

sentences.zh: 行四十日，至福寧，見零，問夫葬地，則榛莽四塞，不可識。

translations.literal: She traveled forty days to Funing, saw Ling, and asked the burial place of her husband; it was overgrown on all sides and could not be recognized.
translations.idiomatic: She traveled forty days to Funing and saw Ling. She asked where her husband was buried, but thorns and brush blocked it on every side and it could not be recognized.

sentences.zh: 張哀慟欲絕。

translations.literal: Zhang grieved and wailed until near death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang grieved and wailed until she nearly died.

sentences.zh: 夫忽降於童，言動無異其生時，告張死時事，甚悲，且指示骨所在處。

translations.literal: Her husband suddenly descended upon a boy; his speech and movements were no different from when he lived, and he told Zhang the circumstances of his death, very sorrowfully, and also indicated where the bones lay.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband suddenly appeared through a boy. His speech and movements were no different from when he lived. He told Zhang how he had died, full of sorrow, and showed her where the bones lay.

sentences.zh: 張如其言發得之，持骨祝曰：「爾信妾夫耶？

translations.literal: Zhang as he said dug and obtained them; she held the bones and prayed: "Are you truly my husband?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang dug as he said and found them. She held the bones and prayed, "Are you truly my husband?

sentences.zh: 入口當如冰雪，黏如膠。」

translations.literal: If you enter my mouth they should be like ice and snow, sticky like glue."
translations.idiomatic: If you enter my mouth they should be cold as ice and snow and sticky as glue."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Afterward it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward it was indeed so.

sentences.zh: 官義之，上於大府，使零護喪還，給錢使葬，仍旌門，復其役。

translations.literal: The officials praised her righteousness and reported upward to the great prefecture; they had Ling escort the coffin back, gave money for burial, still erected an honorific gate, and remitted their corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The officials praised her righteousness and reported to the great prefecture. Ling was sent to escort the coffin home, money was given for burial, an honorific gate was erected, and their corvée was remitted.

sentences.zh: 丁氏，新建鄭伯文妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Ding was the wife of Zheng Bowen of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ding was the wife of Zheng Bowen of Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 大德間，伯文病將歿，丁氏與訣曰：「妾自得侍巾櫛，誓與偕老。

translations.literal: During Dade Bowen was gravely ill and about to die; Ding took leave saying: "Since I obtained the honor of serving at your side I vowed to grow old together.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era Bowen fell gravely ill. Ding took leave of him, saying, "Since I obtained the honor of serving at your side I vowed to grow old together.

sentences.zh: 君今不幸疾若是，脫有不諱，妾當從。

translations.literal: Now you are unfortunately ill thus; if something cannot be avoided I should follow you.
translations.idiomatic: Now you are so gravely ill. If the worst cannot be avoided I should follow you.

sentences.zh: 但君父母已老，無他子婦侍養，妾苟復自亡，使君父母食不甘味，則君亦不瞑目矣。

translations.literal: But your parents are already old and there is no other son or daughter-in-law to serve them; if I again destroy myself your parents will eat without savor—then you too will not close your eyes in peace.
translations.idiomatic: But your parents are already old and there is no other son or daughter-in-law to serve them. If I destroy myself as well your parents will eat without savor—and you too will not rest in peace.

sentences.zh: 妾且忍死，以奉其餘年，必不改事他人，以負君於冥冥也。」

translations.literal: I shall for the time being endure death to serve their remaining years; I will certainly not marry another to betray you in the hidden realm."
translations.idiomatic: I shall endure living for now to serve their remaining years. I will certainly not marry another and betray you in the world beyond."

sentences.zh: 伯文卒，丁氏年二十七，居喪哀毀。

translations.literal: Bowen died; Ding was twenty-seven and dwelt in mourning with destroyed grief.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen died. Ding was twenty-seven and mourned with utter devastation.

sentences.zh: 服既除，父母屢議奪嫁之，丁氏每聞必慟哭曰：「妾所以不死者，非苟生有他志也，與良人約，將以事舅姑耳。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed her parents repeatedly discussed forcing her to remarry; each time Ding heard she must wail: "The reason I do not die is not that I cling to life with another intent—I made a pact with my good man to serve his parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was completed her parents repeatedly urged her to remarry. Each time Ding heard it she wailed, "The reason I do not die is not that I cling to life with another intent. I made a pact with my husband to serve his parents.

sentences.zh: 今舅姑在堂固無恙，妾可棄去而不信於良人乎！」

translations.literal: Now my parents-in-law are in the hall and are still well—how can I abandon them and be faithless to my good man!"
translations.idiomatic: Now my parents-in-law are still well. How can I abandon them and be faithless to my husband!"

sentences.zh: 父遂止。

translations.literal: Her father then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Her father then stopped.

sentences.zh: 舅姑嘗病，丁氏夙夜護視，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: When her parents-in-law were ill Ding watched day and night, her garments never unfastened.
translations.idiomatic: When her parents-in-law fell ill Ding watched day and night without unfastening her garments.

sentences.zh: 及死，喪葬盡禮。

translations.literal: When they died burial and mourning were fully according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When they died she observed burial and mourning in full according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 事上，表其門。

translations.literal: Reported upward, her gate was commended.
translations.idiomatic: The case was reported upward and her gate was commended.

sentences.zh: 白氏，太原人。

translations.literal: Bai was from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 夫慕釋氏道，棄家為僧。

translations.literal: Her husband admired the Buddhist path, abandoned the household and became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband admired the Buddhist path, abandoned the household, and became a monk.

sentences.zh: 白氏年二十，留養姑不去，服勤績紝，以供租賦。

translations.literal: Bai was twenty, remained to nourish her mother-in-law and did not leave, served diligently at spinning hemp to supply rent and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Bai was twenty. She remained to support her mother-in-law and did not leave, working diligently at spinning to supply rent and taxes.

sentences.zh: 夫一日還，迫使他適，白斷發誓不從，夫不能奪，乃去。

translations.literal: One day her husband returned and forced her to remarry; Bai cut her hair and swore she would not comply; her husband could not compel her and then left.
translations.idiomatic: One day her husband returned and tried to force her to remarry. Bai cut her hair and swore she would not comply. Her husband could not compel her and left.

sentences.zh: 姑年九十卒，竭力營葬，畫姑像祀之終身。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law died at ninety she exhausted her strength to arrange burial and painted her mother-in-law's portrait to worship for life.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law died at ninety she exhausted her strength to arrange the burial and painted her portrait to worship for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 趙美妻王氏，內黃人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Zhao Mei, was from Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, wife of Zhao Mei, was from Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，美溺水死，王氏誓守忠，舅姑念其年少無子，欲使更適人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi Mei drowned and died; Wang swore to keep faith; her parents-in-law, pitying her youth and lack of a son, wished her to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi Mei drowned and died. Wang swore to keep her faith. Her parents-in-law, pitying her youth and lack of a son, wished her to remarry.

sentences.zh: 王氏曰：「婦義無再醮，且舅姑在，妾可棄而去耶！」

translations.literal: Wang said: "A wife by righteousness does not remarry; moreover my parents-in-law are alive—how can I abandon them and leave!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang said, "A wife by righteousness does not remarry. Moreover my parents-in-law are alive—how can I abandon them and leave!"

sentences.zh: 舅姑乃欲以族侄與繼婚，王氏拒不從。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law then wished to have a clan nephew marry her in succession; Wang refused and would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law then wished to have a clan nephew marry her in succession. Wang refused.

sentences.zh: 舅姑迫之力，王氏知不免，即引繩自經死。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law pressed her with force; Wang knew she could not escape and took a rope and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law pressed her hard. Wang knew she could not escape, took a rope, and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 李冬兒，甄城人，丁從信妻也。

translations.literal: Li Dong'er was from Zhencheng and was the wife of Ding Congxin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dong'er was from Zhencheng and was the wife of Ding Congxin.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，從信歿，服闋，父母呼歸問之，曰：「汝年少居孀，又無子，何以自立，吾為汝再擇婿何如？」

translations.literal: At twenty-three Congxin died; when mourning was completed her parents called her home and asked: "You are young and widowed and have no son—how will you support yourself? Shall we choose another husband for you?"
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-three Congxin died. When mourning was completed her parents called her home and asked, "You are young, widowed, and have no son. How will you support yourself? Shall we find another husband for you?"

sentences.zh: 冬兒不從，詣從信塚哭，欲縊墓樹上，家人防之，不果。
